headline: UK Energy Price Cap Rises 26% in January Amid Higher Wholesale Costs
summary: Energy prices for UK households will surge by 26% from January 1, bringing the average bill in Great Britain to £2,166 annually. The energy regulator Ofgem stated the increase is driven by higher wholesale gas prices stemming from the Middle East war.
why: The UK energy price cap protects household consumers by limiting the maximum unit rates and standing charges utility suppliers can charge on standard variable tariffs.

impacts.name: Utilities
impacts.why: Higher price caps allow UK utility providers to pass increased wholesale gas costs on to consumers.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The 26% jump in the UK energy price cap directly reflects surging wholesale gas costs driven by geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
